title: Savitri
hook: Savitri has no weapon and no army on the road behind Death, only a conversation

segments.voice: Yesterday, Savitri in the hermitage, carrying Narada's warning alone and counting the days. Your line was Savitri. Were you gentle with someone carrying something you couldn't see? Day one thousand three hundred forty-four.

No sword. No army. No spell. When Yama, the lord of death, draws Satyavan's life out of his body and turns south, Savitri has nothing to fight with. What she has is a voice, and she uses it. She walks behind Death and talks. And Death, again and again, stops to listen. Last year we followed the boons one by one. Today we listen to what she actually says, because that's what moves him.
screen: `NO SWORD, NO ARMY.` → `SHE WALKS AND TALKS.` → `DEATH STOPS TO LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Yama tells her to turn back. Her first answer is about where she belongs: where her husband is taken, she goes. Then she says something about friendship. The wise say, she tells him, that walking seven steps together makes people friends. She has walked more than that beside him. So, as a friend, let him hear her. Notice the move. She doesn't plead with Death as an enemy. She claims him as a companion on the road. Then she speaks of dharma, the right way, and of the good, the people who keep to it. Yama is pleased and offers a gift, anything but Satyavan's life. She asks for her father-in-law's sight. She keeps talking: being near the good, even for a moment, is never wasted. Another gift: her father-in-law's kingdom. She speaks of how the good are kind even to those who wrong them. Another gift: sons for her own father. And then the good, she says, hold the world up by their truth. Each time, Yama is pleased, and each time, what pleases him is not grief and not cleverness. It's what she says about goodness. Some retellings make it a story of Savitri outwitting Death. The epic tells it more like a conversation that Death enjoys. She praises the good to the one who judges everyone, and she means it. Now step back, because this is a week's end. The week opened with Kunti, then three days with Gandhari: an honest blessing, a folded cloth, a night by the river. And then three with Savitri: her name, her silence, and now her voice. Three women, each holding on with what she had.
screen: `SEVEN STEPS MAKE A FRIEND` · `THE GOOD, AND BEING NEAR THEM` · `KIND EVEN TO THOSE WHO WRONG THEM` · `A CONVERSATION DEATH ENJOYS`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: bring a good person to mind. Settle, and let the breath find its own pace. Call up someone whose goodness you've seen up close, not famous, just good. Remember one small kind thing they did, something nobody else noticed. Stay near them for a moment, the way Savitri says the good are worth being near. Let that one memory be enough. If you pray, you can give thanks for them. The bell holds the time.
Savitri. The woman who walked behind Death and spoke about the good until he gave her what she asked. Today's word.
Your line: Savitri. Today, say something good about a good person, out loud, to someone else. Day one thousand three hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Hindus hear Savitri's words to Yama when her story is read or retold, in the Mahabharata's forest book, at home, in temple talks, and on the day of the vow some married women keep in her name.

fork.setup: you're walking behind Death, and he tells you to turn back. what do you say first?
options: beg him to take you instead.
tell him where your husband goes, you go, and call him a friend.
fork.reveal: she says she goes where her husband is taken, and that seven steps together make people friends. Death stops to listen.

original.note: Sanskrit: the princess's name, the same as the goddess who granted her birth and the verse to the sun god Savitr.

trapdoor: what you thought: Savitri tricked Death.
what it means: she spoke of friendship, dharma and the good, and he was pleased each time.
what a scholar hears: in the epic, every gift follows a speech about the good, and the first three go to her elders before she asks anything for herself.
recall: names what was in her power

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva (Savitri follows Yama; seven steps and friendship; her speeches on dharma and the good; the boons for her father-in-law and father)

notes: Week end: the look-back names Kunti (day 1338), Gandhari (1339–1341) and Savitri (1342–1344). Days 1338–1341 were not on disk when this was written; check the Gandhari summary ('chose blindness beside her husband') matches those days.

Year 3 day 799 walked through the same boons; this day centers on the content of her speeches. Confirm the order and wording of the paraphrased teachings (seven steps and friendship; dharma; the company of the good is never fruitless; the good are kind even to enemies; the good uphold the world by truth).
'A conversation Death enjoys' is interpretive (the epic repeats that Yama is pleased). Keeper may soften.
Some retellings frame the boons as a trick; the script attributes that to retellings, not to the epic.

Editor pass: trapdoor corrected (the fourth boon, sons by Satyavan, is also for her, so 'only the last one is for her' was wrong); stock lines cut ('easy to miss on a first hearing', 'that's the heart of it'); week-end look-back now names what the Gandhari days covered.
